newsitem.title: NORWAY: Aker/RGI merged group revenues about NOK 19 bln.
newsitem.headline: Aker/RGI merged group revenues about NOK 19 bln.

text.p: Norwegian engineering and offshore group Aker ASA said on Tuesday the fusion with investment group Resource Group International (RGI) would form a company with annual revenues of about 19 billion crowns and almost 17,000 employees.
"The aim of the merger is to create a powerful Norwegian-based industrial owner with the focus on future growth and value creation," a statement from Aker said.

Core businesses in the merged group, Aker RGI, will initially include oil and gas technology through an 80 percent stake in Aker Maritime, cement and building materials through a one-third holding in Swedish-based Scancem and fish through a 61 percent interest in Norway Seafoods, Aker said.
In September Aker shareholders approved a proposed merger of Aker's Oil and Gas Technology division and offshore supplier Maritime Group to form a new company, Aker Maritime ASA.
"The new group also embraces a number of other operations of varying size with an interesting potential for further development. These include shipbuilding and material handling," the statement said.

Aker chairman Bjoern Rune Gjelsten will be nominated as chairman of the board of the new company. Aker will formally act as the acquiring company and RGI, currently registered in the Netherlands Antilles, will transfer operations to Norway.

Majority RGI shareholder Kjell Inge Roekke will be the largest shareholder in the new group with 33 percent of the stock. He will play an active role in the seafood business and be a member of the Aker RGI board.
Providing the transaction is approved by the general meetings of the two groups in late November, the merger will take formal effect in early 1997, Aker said.
